1.title: Are close-knit families a thing of the past?
1.brief: Write an opinion essay answering the question: “Are close-knit families disappearing in modern society?” Give arguments for both sides and your conclusion.
1.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre si las familias unidas están desapareciendo, con argumentos y conclusión.
criteria: Five verbs followed by gerunds (avoid, keep, miss, consider, can’t help).
Two noun clauses after “be” (The problem is that…, What matters is whether…).
Four paragraphs with an introduction, two sides and a conclusion.
1.model:
Many people claim that the close-knit family is disappearing. In Colombia, where families have traditionally been large and united, this question is particularly relevant.

On the one hand, modern life makes staying close difficult. Young people often consider moving to big cities or abroad for work, and parents keep working long hours. Many grandparents miss seeing their grandchildren every Sunday. The problem is that technology can replace real contact: a video call is not the same as a family lunch.

On the other hand, families have not stopped caring; they have simply changed. Siblings who live in different countries keep chatting every day on WhatsApp, and many couples avoid moving far from their parents so that they can help with childcare. The truth is that bonding with relatives now takes different forms.

In conclusion, I believe that families are not drifting apart but adapting. What matters is whether we make an effort to be present. I can't help thinking that a family that shares one meal a week is still a close-knit family.

1.title: Patching things up
1.brief: Write an email to a relative or friend after an argument. Apologise, explain your feelings and suggest how to patch things up.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un familiar o amigo después de una discusión: discúlpate y propón cómo reconciliarse.
criteria: Four verbs + gerund, including after a preposition (sorry for shouting, insist on paying).
One noun clause after “be” (The thing is that…).
Use two expressions: to patch things up, to see eye to eye, to rub someone up the wrong way.
1.model:
Dear Tomás,

I've been thinking about our argument at Mom's birthday, and I can't stop feeling bad about it. I'm really sorry for shouting at you in front of everyone. It wasn't fair, and I regret saying those things about your job.

The thing is that I was stressed about work, and when you started criticising my decision to move to Medellín, it rubbed me up the wrong way. I know we don't always see eye to eye, but you're my little brother and I hate fighting with you.

I'd really like to patch things up. How about meeting for lunch next Saturday? I insist on paying — it's the least I can do! We could also consider spending a weekend at the farm together, like we used to when we were kids. I miss talking to you.

Let me know what you think. I promise to listen without interrupting this time.

Love,
Catalina

1.title: The black sheep
1.brief: Write a story about the “black sheep” of a family — a person who was different from everyone else. Show how the family's attitude changed over time.
1.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre la “oveja negra” de una familia y cómo cambió la actitud familiar hacia ella.
criteria: Six gerunds, including two as subjects or after prepositions.
Two noun clauses after “be”.
Use “black sheep”, “to take after” and “to drift apart”.
1.model:
In my mother's family, everyone is a doctor or a lawyer. Everyone, that is, except my uncle Rafael. He was always the black sheep. Instead of studying medicine like his father, he spent his teenage years playing the drums and painting murals on the walls of the house.

My grandparents couldn't stand seeing him "waste his life". The family's biggest fear was that he would end up poor and alone. When he moved to Berlin at twenty-two, he and his parents drifted apart. For almost ten years, nobody mentioned his name at Christmas.

Then, one day, my grandmother saw an article in El Tiempo about a Colombian artist whose work was being exhibited in a famous European gallery. It was Rafael. Seeing his photo in the newspaper changed everything. She called him that same night, and he flew home a month later.

Today my uncle is the most admired person at family gatherings. The irony is that I take after him: I'm studying art, and nobody objects to me following my dreams. Being different, my family learned, is not the same as failing.

1.title: What makes a family?
1.brief: Read 'Four Passports, One Sofa' and look at the multicultural family photo in Unit 1. Write an opinion essay: Are families with members from different countries and cultures an advantage for children, or do they face more problems than benefits? Give reasons and examples.
1.briefEs: Ensayo de opinión: ¿crecer en una familia multicultural es una ventaja o trae más problemas?
criteria: Use at least three verbs followed by gerunds (avoid, imagine, keep, admit…).
Use two noun clauses after be (The problem is that… / The truth is that…).
Organise the essay in introduction, two body paragraphs and conclusion.
Use contrast linkers: however, although, on the other hand.
1.model:
Families whose members come from different countries are becoming increasingly common, and many people wonder whether children benefit from growing up in them. In my opinion, the advantages clearly outweigh the difficulties.

First of all, children in multicultural families usually grow up speaking more than one language. They practise switching between languages every day, so they rarely mind changing from one to another. The truth is that this is a skill many adults spend years trying to learn. They also get used to celebrating different holidays and trying different food, which makes them more open-minded.

On the other hand, these families do face challenges. Parents may keep arguing about traditions, and grandparents sometimes resist accepting a partner from another culture. The problem is that each person brings a different idea of what a normal family is. However, most of these tensions disappear with time, especially when grandchildren are born.

In conclusion, although multicultural families have to negotiate more than others, I can't imagine a better place to learn tolerance. Children who grow up in them learn to see the world from more than one point of view, and that is a lesson no school can easily teach.

1.title: Family meals at school
1.brief: Write a short report for your school on how often students eat with their families. Describe the findings and make recommendations.
1.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve para tu colegio sobre con qué frecuencia los estudiantes comen en familia, con hallazgos y recomendaciones.
criteria: Use at least four verbs followed by gerunds (admit, avoid, keep, suggest, miss).
Use two noun clauses after “be” (The main reason is that…, What matters most is whether…).
Organise the report with headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
1.model:
Report: Family Meals among Year 12 Students

Introduction
This report examines how often students at our school eat with their families, based on a survey of sixty students.

Findings
Most students admit skipping family meals on weekdays. Many avoid eating at home because they finish training late, and several keep working on homework instead. The main reason is that parents and students have different timetables. Surprisingly, only a few students regret missing these meals, although most say they miss talking to their parents. Another finding is that students who eat together at weekends say they feel closer to their relatives.

Recommendations
We suggest organising one shared meal a week. What matters most is whether families can protect that time, so schools should avoid setting homework for Sunday evening. We also recommend considering a short workshop for parents on planning meals.

Conclusion
Shared meals are not impossible, but they need planning. In short, the problem is not a lack of love but a lack of time. The school can help by keeping the weekend free.

1.title: A family day at the community centre
1.brief: Write a proposal to the manager of a community centre for a monthly family day. Explain the current situation and your recommendations.
1.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al director de un centro comunitario para un día familiar mensual, con la situación actual y tus recomendaciones.
criteria: Use at least four verbs followed by gerunds (recommend, enjoy, consider, can’t help…).
Use one noun clause after “be” (The idea is that…, The truth is that…).
Use the headings Introduction, Current situation, Proposal and Conclusion, and formal language throughout.
1.model:
Proposal: A Family Day at the Riverside Community Centre

Introduction
This proposal suggests a monthly family day, based on conversations with twenty local parents.

Current situation
At present, the centre offers activities for children or for adults, but never for both. As a result, many families spend the weekend in separate rooms. Many parents say they can't help feeling guilty about working at weekends, and teenagers rarely join in family events.

Proposal
We recommend organising a free Sunday afternoon with games, cooking and sport. The idea is that grandparents, parents and children take part together. Families would enjoy cooking a simple dish, and teenagers could consider leading the football match. Each month would have a theme, such as music or gardening, so that families keep coming back. Registration would be simple: parents could sign up at reception or online.

Conclusion
The truth is that the cost would be low, because volunteers could run most activities. We look forward to discussing the plan with you.

1.title: Encanto: a film about family pressure
1.brief: Write a review of a film or series about a family. Describe the story, say what you liked and disliked, and give a rating.
1.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una película o serie sobre una familia: la historia, lo que te gustó y lo que no, y una valoración.
criteria: Use at least two verbs followed by gerunds (keep, can’t stop, admit, enjoy…).
Use one noun clause after “be” (The problem is that…, What makes it special is that…).
Use two relative clauses (who, whose or which) and end with a clear rating.
1.model:
Encanto (2021) is an animated film about a Colombian family with a magical house. Every member of the Madrigal family has a special gift, except Mirabel, who feels like an outsider.

What I enjoyed most was the way the film shows family pressure. Mirabel keeps trying to prove that she belongs, and her grandmother, whose strict rules are meant to protect everyone, can't stop worrying about the family's reputation. The problem is that nobody admits feeling tired or afraid. I also liked the music, which is catchy and full of Colombian rhythms.

My only criticism is that some characters have very little time on screen, so a few relatives remain mysterious.

Overall, this is a warm, colourful story about accepting each other's weaknesses. What makes it special is that the real hero is not a person with powers but a girl who listens. I would recommend it to anyone who likes family stories, and I give it four stars out of five.

1.title: Asking for a family discount
1.brief: Write a formal letter to a sports centre asking whether it offers family memberships and requesting some information.
1.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal a un centro deportivo preguntando por membresías familiares y pidiendo información.
criteria: Use at least four verbs followed by gerunds (consider, enjoy, suggest, appreciate, can’t help…).
Use two noun clauses after “be” (The problem is that…, What matters most is that…).
Start with “Dear Sir or Madam” and end with “Yours faithfully”, and include at least two indirect questions.
1.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about family memberships at the Parque Verde Sports Centre. My husband and I have three children, and we are considering joining the centre in January.

At present, your website lists only individual prices, so I would like to know whether you offer a discount for families. The problem is that four separate memberships would be too expensive for us. We enjoy swimming together at weekends, and our oldest son suggests training in the gym on weekdays.

I would also be grateful if you could tell me what the opening hours are on Sundays and whether children under ten may use the pool without an adult. What matters most to us is that all of us can use the facilities at the same time.

I would appreciate receiving a reply by the end of the month, as we cannot help worrying that the January places will be full. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Marta Quintero

1.title: Flexible hours to care for a parent
1.brief: Write an email to your manager asking to change your working hours for a few months because a family member needs care.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a tu jefa pidiendo cambiar tu horario unos meses porque un familiar necesita cuidados.
criteria: Use at least four verbs followed by gerunds (propose, avoid, mind, keep, appreciate…).
Use one noun clause after “be” (The situation is that…, What I am asking for is…).
Use two relative clauses and a polite, professional opening and closing.
1.model:
Dear Ms Herrera,

I am writing to ask whether it would be possible to change my working hours for the next three months. My father is recovering from an operation, and I have been arranging his care with my sister.

The situation is that he needs someone at home between eight and ten in the morning. I would like to propose starting work at ten and finishing at six, and I can make up the time by avoiding long lunch breaks. I do not mind working from home on Fridays, which would also help me manage his appointments.

I understand that the team depends on me during the morning calls, so I have discussed the plan with Pablo, who has offered to cover them. What I am asking for is a temporary arrangement, and I will keep updating you on his recovery.

I would be grateful if we could discuss this on Monday. Thank you for considering my request.

Kind regards,
Daniel Ortiz

1.title: Three generations under one roof
1.brief: Write an article for a youth magazine about living with several generations of your family. Describe the problems and the benefits.
1.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para una revista juvenil sobre vivir con varias generaciones de tu familia: problemas y beneficios.
criteria: Use at least five verbs followed by gerunds (can’t help, insist on, keep, enjoy, avoid, miss, admit…).
Use two noun clauses after “be” (What surprised me most was that…, The truth is that…).
Use one relative clause with “whose” and one non-defining clause with “which”.
1.model:
Three Generations under One Roof

Living with your grandparents is not what most teenagers dream of, but I would not change it. When my parents moved to Cali for work, I could not help feeling nervous about sharing a small flat with my grandmother and grandfather.

At first, the house rules were the problem. My grandfather insisted on having dinner at six, and I kept forgetting to switch off the television. However, we soon discovered that we enjoy talking about the same things: football, old songs and the neighbours' gossip.

What surprised me most was that my grandmother, whose English is limited, wanted to learn it with me. Now we practise every evening, and she avoids using Spanish at the table, which is quite funny.

The truth is that living together is sometimes tiring. I miss having my own room, and I admit complaining about the noise more than once. Nevertheless, I have learned patience and gained two best friends.

If your grandparents live nearby, consider spending more time with them. You might be surprised.

1.title: The reunion
1.brief: Write a short story about a family reunion where an old disagreement is finally put aside.
1.briefEs: Escribe un relato corto sobre una reunión familiar en la que por fin se deja atrás una vieja discusión.
criteria: Use at least four verbs followed by gerunds (stop, admit, avoid, imagine…).
Use two noun clauses after “be” (The reason was that…, What I remember best is that…).
Use two relative clauses with “who” and a clear beginning, problem and resolution.
1.model:
Every August, my family met at my great-aunt's farm near Villa de Leyva, and every August the same argument began: who would cook the lamb? That year, however, my cousin Nicolás refused to come. The reason was that he had stopped speaking to his father three years earlier.

My great-aunt, who never gave up on anyone, phoned him herself. "I can't imagine a reunion without you," she said. Nicolás hesitated, then admitted missing the noise of the kitchen.

He arrived on Saturday afternoon, carrying a bag of oranges. His father, who was chopping onions, stopped working and looked at him. Nobody said a word. Then my great-aunt put a knife in Nicolás's hand and said, "You are cutting the potatoes."

By evening, they were arguing about the lamb. What I remember best is that everyone laughed, including the two of them. The apology never came in words, but I understood that avoiding the subject was their way of saying sorry. Sometimes families repair things by cooking together.

2.title: An unsolved mystery
2.brief: Write an article for a magazine about a famous unsolved mystery (a disappearance, a strange event). Present the facts and speculate about what happened.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre un misterio sin resolver: presenta los hechos y especula sobre lo ocurrido.
criteria: Four modals of certainty about the past (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use “clue”, “baffling”, “to shed light on” and “circumstantial”.
A title, an engaging introduction and a personal conclusion.
2.model:
The Ship That Vanished

In 1925, the SS Cotopaxi left Charleston for Havana with 32 crew members. It never arrived. For almost a century, its disappearance was one of the most baffling mysteries of the sea.

Some people believed that the ship must have been destroyed in the Bermuda Triangle by forces nobody could explain. However, that theory can't have been true: there is no scientific evidence for such forces. Others thought the crew might have abandoned the ship after a mutiny, but no survivors ever appeared.

In 2020, researchers finally shed light on the case. They found a wreck off the coast of Florida that matched the Cotopaxi's description. The clues suggested that the ship could have sunk in a sudden storm; old records show that a tropical storm hit the area the day after it sailed. Some experts warn that the evidence is circumstantial, because the name of the ship was not visible on the wreck.

In my opinion, the storm theory is the most convincing. The ship must have been overloaded, and the captain should have waited for better weather. Sometimes, the simplest explanation is the right one.

2.title: I should have known better
2.brief: Write an email to a friend about a mistake you made recently. Explain what you had to do, what you should have done and what you didn't need to do.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre un error reciente: lo que tuviste que hacer y lo que deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Use had to, should have, didn’t need to / needn’t have and was supposed to.
Two speculations about the past (must have, might have).
Use “in hindsight” and “to jump to conclusions”.
2.model:
Hi Sofía,

You won't believe what happened last week. I was supposed to present a report to the directors on Friday, so I stayed up until 3 a.m. on Thursday finishing it. When I arrived at the office, my boss told me the meeting had been cancelled. I needn't have worked all night! Someone must have sent an email, but I never received it. It might have gone to my spam folder.

Then I made it worse. I jumped to conclusions and accused my colleague Andrés of not telling me on purpose. I had to apologise to him in front of the whole team, which was embarrassing. In hindsight, I should have checked my inbox before getting angry, and I shouldn't have assumed the worst about him.

The good news is that the meeting is next Tuesday, so I didn't need to rewrite anything. Lesson learned: always check your spam!

Big hug,
Valentina

2.title: Review of a mystery film or book
2.brief: Write a review of a mystery film, series or book. Describe the plot without spoiling the ending, speculate about the characters and give your recommendation.
2.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una película, serie o libro de misterio sin revelar el final y da tu recomendación.
criteria: Three past modals of deduction about the characters or plot.
Use four words from the unit: eerie, clue, culprit, to figure out, to overlook.
Recommendation with a clear rating or verdict.
2.model:
Knives Out (2019) is one of the most entertaining mystery films of recent years. The story begins when Harlan Thrombey, a wealthy crime novelist, is found dead the morning after his 85th birthday party. The police think he must have taken his own life, but a private detective, Benoit Blanc, is not so sure.

What makes the film gripping is that every member of the family seems to have a motive. One of them might have killed him for money; another could have wanted revenge. As the clues appear, you start trying to figure out who the culprit is, and the director plays with your expectations brilliantly. Several times I thought, "It can't have been her!" — and I changed my mind ten minutes later.

The atmosphere in the old house is eerie, but the film is also very funny, thanks to the excellent cast. My only criticism is that one or two details are easy to overlook, so you need to pay attention.

Overall, I would definitely recommend it, especially to people who love classic detective stories. It's clever, stylish and full of surprises. I give it four and a half stars out of five.

2.title: Missing laptops in Room 14
2.brief: Write an incident report for the head teacher about three laptops that disappeared from a locked classroom. State the facts, say what may have happened and make recommendations.
2.briefEs: Escribe un informe de incidente para la directora sobre tres portátiles que desaparecieron de un aula cerrada: hechos, hipótesis y recomendaciones.
criteria: Use at least four modals of deduction about the past (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use the headings Introduction, Facts, Analysis, Recommendations and Conclusion.
Use one past modal of criticism (should have) and a formal, impersonal tone.
2.model:
Incident Report: Missing Laptops in Room 14

Introduction
This report describes the disappearance of three laptops from Room 14 on Thursday and suggests what may have happened.

Facts
The laptops were last seen at three. The room was locked at half past three and found open at eight on Friday morning. There is no sign of forced entry.

Analysis
Someone must have used a key, because the lock is undamaged. The cleaner can't have taken them, as she was on holiday that week. The security guard might have forgotten to lock the door, which could have given a thief the opportunity. It is also possible that a teacher moved the laptops to another room and didn't tell anyone.

Recommendations
We should have kept a record of who borrows keys. From now on, every key should be signed for, and the cameras should be checked before the end of the week.

Conclusion
The evidence is inconclusive, but a lack of control over the keys is the most likely cause.

2.title: A parcel that arrived broken
2.brief: Write a formal letter of complaint to an online shop about a parcel that arrived late and damaged. Explain what was supposed to happen, what went wrong and what you request.
2.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de queja a una tienda en línea por un paquete que llegó tarde y roto: lo previsto, lo que falló y lo que pides.
criteria: Use was supposed to, had to, should have and needn’t have.
Use two modals of speculation about the past (must have, might have).
Start with “Dear Sir or Madam”, end with “Yours faithfully” and state a clear request.
2.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about an order (number 58213) that I placed on 4 October for a desk lamp.

According to your website, the parcel was supposed to arrive within three working days. It arrived ten days later, and the box was crushed. The courier must have dropped it, because the lamp was broken in two pieces. I had to take a day off work to receive the delivery, which I needn't have done if you had told me about the delay.

Your customer service team should have contacted me as soon as the problem appeared. Instead, I had to phone three times, and nobody could explain what had happened. The first adviser might have misunderstood my address, since she asked me for it twice.

I therefore request a full refund, as I no longer wish to receive a replacement. I would also like an explanation of how you intend to avoid similar errors. If I do not hear from you within fourteen days, I will contact a consumer organisation.

Yours faithfully,
Inés Palacios

2.title: Can eyewitnesses be trusted?
2.brief: Write an argumentative essay on whether the memory of an eyewitness is reliable enough to be used as evidence in a court of law.
2.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo argumentativo sobre si la memoria de un testigo presencial es lo bastante fiable como prueba judicial.
criteria: Use at least four modals of deduction about the past (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use at least two linkers (First, On the other hand, even though, In conclusion).
Organise the essay in an introduction, two body paragraphs and a conclusion with your opinion.
2.model:
Imagine that you see a robbery and, a week later, the police ask you to describe the thief. How reliable would your memory be? In my opinion, eyewitnesses are far less trustworthy than most people believe.

First, memory is influenced by stress. A witness who saw a crime for a few seconds can't have noticed every detail, and fear might have changed what he or she remembers. Questions can also shape answers. If an officer asks, "Was the man tall?", the witness may later recall a tall man even though he could have been of average height.

On the other hand, eyewitnesses are sometimes essential. When there are no cameras, their words may be the only evidence. A careful interview, carried out soon after the event, has a better chance of producing accurate information than one conducted months later.

In conclusion, eyewitness testimony should never be used alone. Courts ought to compare it with physical evidence, because a confident witness can still be wrong. Witnesses who identify the wrong person must have sincerely believed their memory, which makes the problem worse.

2.title: The open door
2.brief: Write a short story in which someone finds a shop or office in a strange state and works out what must have happened.
2.briefEs: Escribe un relato en el que alguien encuentra un local en un estado extraño y deduce qué debió de pasar.
criteria: Use at least four modals of deduction about the past (must have, couldn’t have, might have, could have).
Use was supposed to, should have and needn’t have once each.
Include a clear beginning, a mystery and a resolution, with dialogue.
2.model:
On Monday morning, Elena arrived at the bakery and found the door wide open. Inside, the lights were on, the till was empty and a half-eaten sandwich lay on the counter.

"Someone must have broken in," she thought. But the window was intact, and the alarm hadn't gone off. A burglar couldn't have entered without a key. She remembered that her brother Hugo had asked to borrow the keys the week before. He might have come in to collect some flour, or he could have forgotten to lock up after helping her on Saturday.

She phoned him. "I was supposed to tell you," he admitted. "I needed to pick up the flour on Sunday, and I took the money from the till to pay the driver. I should have left a note."

Elena was furious for a minute, then she laughed. The sandwich, it turned out, was his lunch. "You needn't have taken the whole day's money," she said, "but next time, please write a note."

2.title: Apologising to a client
2.brief: Write an email to a client apologising for sending the wrong document. Explain what you were supposed to do, what went wrong and what will change.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un cliente disculpándote por enviar un documento equivocado: lo que debías hacer, lo que falló y lo que cambiará.
criteria: Use was supposed to, should have, had to and needn’t have.
Use two modals of speculation about the past (must have, might have).
Use “in hindsight” and a polite, professional opening and closing.
2.model:
Dear Mr Alvarez,

Thank you for your message about the invoice we sent on Tuesday. I am sorry for the confusion and the extra work it caused you.

I was supposed to send you the revised quote, but I attached an old invoice instead. In hindsight, I should have checked the attachment before pressing "send". I might have been distracted because I was working on two projects at once, and I must have opened the wrong folder.

I understand that you had to call your accountant to explain the old figure, which you needn't have done if our message had been clearer. I regret the inconvenience.

I have attached the correct invoice, which shows the price we agreed in June. From now on, a colleague will check every document before it is sent. Please let me know if you would like to discuss the matter by phone. I am very grateful for your patience.

Kind regards,
Rosa Medina

2.title: Preventing double-booked meeting rooms
2.brief: Write a proposal to your manager to stop meeting rooms from being double-booked. Describe the current situation, analyse what went wrong and recommend changes.
2.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a tu gerente para evitar que se reserven dos veces las salas de reuniones: situación actual, análisis y recomendaciones.
criteria: Use the headings Introduction, Current situation, Recommendations and Conclusion.
Use should have, might have and can’t have to analyse the problem.
Use was supposed to and needn’t, and one third conditional in the conclusion.
2.model:
Proposal: Preventing Double-Booked Meeting Rooms

Introduction
This proposal aims to reduce the number of meetings that were double-booked last month, which caused delays and complaints.

Current situation
Eleven meetings had to be moved to other rooms. As a result, staff lost an average of twenty minutes each time. The booking system should have warned staff about the clash, but it only shows a small red mark. Some employees might have ignored the warning, and others can't have noticed it at all because it appears at the bottom of the screen.

Recommendations
Firstly, the system should display a clear alert before a booking is confirmed. Secondly, staff who were supposed to cancel unused rooms should receive a reminder by email. Finally, the front desk needn't check every booking by hand once the new alert is working.

Conclusion
These changes are simple and inexpensive. If they had been introduced earlier, many meetings wouldn't have been moved. I would be glad to present the plan to the management team.

2.title: The riddle of the Nazca lines
2.brief: Write a magazine article about a historical or archaeological riddle that has never been fully explained. Present what is known and speculate about the rest.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de revista sobre un enigma histórico o arqueológico sin explicar del todo: lo que se sabe y tus hipótesis.
criteria: Use at least four modals of deduction about the past (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use one modal of criticism (should have) and a title.
End with a personal opinion that answers the question in the introduction.
2.model:
The Riddle of the Nazca Lines

In the dry desert of southern Peru, huge drawings of animals and shapes cover the ground. The hummingbird, the monkey and the spider are so large that they are best seen from the air. Who made them, and why?

Archaeologists agree that they were made by the Nazca people more than a thousand years ago. They must have used simple tools, such as wooden sticks and ropes, because no machines existed then. However, nobody knows what the lines were for. They might have been part of religious ceremonies, or they could have marked the way to sources of water in a very dry land. Others believe they can't have been roads, since many of the figures are too large to walk around easily.

One thing is certain: the climate has protected them. Little rain and almost no wind have kept the surface intact.

Personally, I find the water theory the most convincing. Whoever drew them should have left a written explanation, but perhaps the silence is part of their charm.

3.title: Off the beaten track
3.brief: Write a travel article about a little-known town or neighbourhood in Colombia that you think tourists should visit.
3.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de viajes sobre un pueblo o barrio poco conocido de Colombia que valga la pena visitar.
criteria: Three relative clauses, at least one non-defining with commas.
Two noun phrases with modifiers in the correct order (a charming little colonial town).
Two contrast connectors (although, whereas, despite, however) and three words from the unit.
3.model:
Barichara: Colombia's Best-Kept Secret

Most tourists who visit Santander head straight for the adventure sports of San Gil. However, just forty minutes away lies Barichara, a quaint little colonial town that many travellers miss.

Barichara, which was declared a national monument in 1978, is steeped in history. Its cobbled streets are lined with beautiful old whitewashed houses with orange tile roofs. Although the town is small, there is plenty to do. You can walk the Camino Real, an ancient stone path that leads to the village of Guane, where you can see fossils embedded in the walls. The town's main square, which is dominated by a huge sandstone cathedral, is the perfect place to soak up the atmosphere.

Whereas Cartagena is bustling and often crowded, Barichara is peaceful. Despite its growing popularity, it has kept its traditional charm, and new hotels have been built in the same architectural style.

If you want to get off the beaten track, Barichara is definitely worth a detour. Go midweek, try the famous hormigas culonas if you're brave, and don't forget your camera.

3.title: City life or small-town life?
3.brief: Write an essay comparing life in a big city with life in a small town. Which is better for young people?
3.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo comparando la vida en una gran ciudad con la de un pueblo: ¿cuál es mejor para los jóvenes?
criteria: Four contrast connectors (while, whereas, although, on the other hand, nevertheless).
Two defining and one non-defining relative clause.
Use “bustling”, “sprawling” and “vibrant”.
3.model:
For young people, choosing where to live is one of the most important decisions they make. While big cities offer opportunities, small towns offer a quality of life that is hard to find elsewhere.

There is no doubt that cities attract young people. A sprawling capital like Bogotá, which has dozens of universities and thousands of companies, provides options that a small town cannot match. The nightlife is vibrant and the cultural scene is rich. Nevertheless, life in the city has serious disadvantages. Rents are high, commutes can take hours, and the bustling streets can make people feel lonely.

Small towns, on the other hand, are safer and more relaxed. People who grow up in them often have strong friendships and a sense of community. Although jobs are scarce, remote work has changed this, and many professionals now work for city companies from rural areas. Whereas a city apartment might be tiny, a house in a town often has a garden.

In my view, cities are better for young people who are studying or starting their careers. However, once they want to settle down, a small town may be the wiser choice.

3.title: Welcome to my neighbourhood
3.brief: Write a short guide to your neighbourhood for newcomers. Describe its landmarks, places to eat and its good and bad points.
3.briefEs: Escribe una guía corta de tu barrio para recién llegados: lugares emblemáticos, dónde comer y pros y contras.
criteria: Correct order of three or more modifiers before a noun.
Three relative clauses (where, which, whose).
One sentence with “a stone’s throw from” and one contrast connector.
3.model:
A Newcomer's Guide to La Candelaria

La Candelaria, which is the historic centre of Bogotá, is a fascinating place to live. It's a stone's throw from the main museums, and the Plaza de Bolívar, where most political protests take place, is only five minutes away.

The neighbourhood is full of narrow old cobbled streets and brightly painted colonial houses. One landmark you shouldn't miss is the Chorro de Quevedo, a small square where the city was supposedly founded. For food, try La Puerta Falsa, a tiny traditional café whose tamales are famous. If you prefer something modern, there are lots of trendy new restaurants that have sprung up near the universities.

Although the area is lively during the day, it becomes quiet at night, and some streets can feel unsafe after dark. You should also be prepared for noise, as street musicians play almost everywhere. Nevertheless, if you love history and culture, there's no better place in the city.

3.title: Casa del Río: a hostel in the coffee region
3.brief: Write a review of a hostel or small hotel in a town you have visited. Describe the place, the good and bad points, and give a rating.
3.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un hostal o pequeño hotel de un pueblo que visitaste: descripción, puntos buenos y malos, y una valoración.
criteria: Use at least three relative clauses, including one non-defining clause with commas.
Use two noun phrases with several modifiers in the correct order (a bright, spacious attic).
Use at least three contrast connectors (however, although, despite, whereas) and end with a rating.
3.model:
Casa del Río: a lovely hostel in Jardín

Casa del Río, which opened two years ago, is a lovely old family house in the coffee region. Our room was a bright, spacious attic with a wooden balcony that looked over the mountains.

The owners, who are both from the town, give guests a friendly welcome and a map of the best local walks. Breakfast is excellent: fresh fruit, eggs and the strong dark coffee that the region is famous for.

However, the hostel is not perfect. Despite the lovely views, the walls are thin, and we could hear the guests next door until midnight. Although the bathroom was spotless, the hot water ran out twice.

Whereas other hostels in town charge extra for the tours, here the guides are included in the price, which is excellent value.

Overall, it is a great choice for travellers who want an authentic experience, and I would happily stay again. Four stars out of five.

3.title: A cycle route along the old railway
3.brief: Write a proposal to the town council for a new tourist or leisure project that would improve your area, such as a cycle route.
3.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al ayuntamiento para un nuevo proyecto turístico o de ocio que mejore tu zona, como una ruta en bicicleta.
criteria: Use the headings Introduction, Current situation, Proposal and Conclusion.
Use at least three relative clauses (that, which, whose, who, where), one of them non-defining.
Use two contrast connectors (although, despite, however, whereas) and at least one noun phrase with three modifiers.
3.model:
Proposal: A Cycle Route along the Old Railway Line

Introduction
This proposal recommends turning the abandoned railway line that connects our town with the lake into a cycle route.

Current situation
The line, which has not been used for thirty years, is overgrown with weeds. Although many visitors come for the lake, most of them arrive by car, and local residents say the narrow main road is dangerous for cyclists.

Proposal
We suggest creating a smooth, four-kilometre path with benches and a small café at the halfway point, where cyclists could rest. The path would be wide enough for two bicycles to pass safely, and lighting could be added near the town. Local schools whose pupils need safe routes would also benefit. Volunteers who live nearby have already offered to help clear the land.

Conclusion
Despite the initial cost, the route would attract tourists and improve public health. However, the main benefit would be a safer town for everyone. We would be happy to provide a detailed budget.

3.title: A tour that was not as advertised
3.brief: Write a formal letter of complaint to a tour company about a guided trip that was very different from the one in the brochure. Request a partial refund.
3.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de queja a una agencia por una excursión guiada muy distinta a la del folleto, y solicita un reembolso parcial.
criteria: Use at least three relative clauses, including two non-defining clauses with commas.
Use at least two contrast connectors (however, although, whereas, despite).
Start with “Dear Sir or Madam”, end with “Yours faithfully” and state a clear request.
3.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the guided tour of the Coffee Region that I booked with your company for 12 March.

The brochure promised a small group, an experienced local guide and lunch at a traditional farm. However, the group had more than thirty people, and the guide, whose English was very poor, could not answer our questions. Although the farm was beautiful, lunch was a cold sandwich eaten on the bus.

I raised these problems with the coach driver, who said that he had no authority to give refunds. I then emailed your office, which has not replied after two weeks.

Whereas I understand that unexpected problems can happen, this tour was very different from the one advertised. I therefore request a partial refund of half the price. I would also appreciate an explanation of why the group size was not respected.

I look forward to your reply within ten days.

Yours faithfully,
Julián Cárdenas

3.title: A free day for a visiting colleague
3.brief: Write an email to a foreign colleague who is visiting your city, suggesting a plan for a free day. Describe the places and warn about any problems.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo a una colega extranjera que visita tu ciudad, proponiendo un plan para un día libre y avisando de posibles problemas.
criteria: Use at least three relative clauses (where, who, whose, that), including one non-defining clause with commas.
Use two noun phrases with several modifiers in the correct order (a huge green nature reserve).
Use at least two contrast connectors (although, however, whereas) and a polite professional opening and closing.
3.model:
Dear Ms Johansson,

I am delighted that you will visit our Medellín office next month. As you asked, here is a short plan for your free day.

In the morning, I suggest a walk through Comuna 13, where colourful murals cover the steep, narrow streets. Although the area is touristy, a local guide, who can explain the history, makes the visit much more meaningful. For lunch, there is a small traditional restaurant whose bandeja paisa is famous.

In the afternoon, you could take the cable car up to Parque Arví, a huge green nature reserve that is only thirty minutes from the centre. However, the weather changes quickly, so please bring a light waterproof jacket. I have tried to include places that are easy to reach by metro.

Whereas the city centre is noisy and busy, the park is quiet and refreshing, so it is ideal after a long flight.

Please let me know if you prefer a different plan.

Kind regards,
Sergio Vélez

3.title: Visitor survey at the Saturday market
3.brief: Write a report on a survey of visitors to a local market or attraction. Present the findings and recommend improvements.
3.briefEs: Escribe un informe sobre una encuesta a visitantes de un mercado o atractivo local: resultados y mejoras recomendadas.
criteria: Use the headings Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
Use at least three relative clauses (who, which, where, that), one of them non-defining.
Use at least three contrast connectors (although, whereas, despite, however).
3.model:
Report: Visitor Survey at the Saturday Market

Introduction
This report presents the results of a survey of eighty visitors to the Saturday market in the old town.

Findings
Most visitors, who came from other regions, said that the market was a lively, authentic place. Although the stalls offer excellent local food, many people complained that there were too few seats. Whereas younger visitors liked the live music, older visitors found it too loud. Only twelve people mentioned the prices, and all of them thought they were fair. Despite the crowds, nearly everyone said they would come again.

Recommendations
We recommend adding a shaded seating area where visitors can eat, and moving the stage to the far end of the square, which is quieter. The council should also publish a simple bilingual map that shows the toilets and exits.

Conclusion
The market, which has existed for decades, is clearly an important part of the town's identity. However popular it is, a few small changes would make it more comfortable for everyone.

3.title: The wrong bus
3.brief: Write a short story about getting lost on your first days in a new city and the person who helped you.
3.briefEs: Escribe un relato corto sobre perderte en tus primeros días en una ciudad nueva y la persona que te ayudó.
criteria: Use at least four relative clauses, including two non-defining clauses with commas.
Use two noun phrases with several modifiers in the correct order (a noisy, crowded neighbourhood).
Use at least three contrast connectors (although, whereas, however, despite).
3.model:
When I arrived in Bogotá to study, I was a nervous eighteen-year-old who had never left my small town. On my first Saturday, I decided to find the university, which was supposed to be only twenty minutes away by bus.

I took the wrong bus, which carried me to a noisy, crowded neighbourhood that I had never heard of. Although I felt lost, I was too proud to ask for help. Then it began to rain.

I ran into a small old café, whose owner, a cheerful woman called Doña Rosa, gave me hot chocolate and a towel. She drew me a map on a napkin, whereas my phone showed only a blank screen because the battery had died.

I reached the university two hours late. However, I did not mind. Despite the rain and my mistake, I had found the first friendly face in the city.

I still visit Doña Rosa every month, and she always asks me if I know where I am going.

4.title: Are you a morning person?
4.brief: Write a magazine article about early birds and night owls. Explain the differences and give advice to each type.
4.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de revista sobre las personas madrugadoras y nocturnas, con consejos para cada tipo.
criteria: Three reduced time clauses (After waking up, Before going to bed, While working).
Three clauses of reason or condition (as long as, since, unless, provided that).
Four idioms from the unit (hit the sack, burn the midnight oil, wind down…).
4.model:
Early Bird or Night Owl?

Some people jump out of bed at 5 a.m., full of energy. Others can barely open their eyes before ten. Scientists say these differences are partly genetic, so there's no point feeling guilty about your natural rhythm.

Early birds are at their most productive in the morning. After waking up, they often exercise or work on important tasks. Since their energy drops in the afternoon, they tend to hit the sack early. If you're a morning person, plan your most difficult work before lunch. However, don't neglect your social life unless you want to miss every party!

Night owls, on the other hand, feel groggy and sluggish in the morning but come alive at night. Many of them burn the midnight oil while studying or creating. The problem is that schools and offices are designed for early risers. As long as you get seven or eight hours of sleep, being a night owl is not unhealthy. Before going to bed, though, it's important to wind down without screens.

Whatever your type, the key is consistency. Provided that you sleep and wake at similar times every day, your body will thank you.

4.title: A routine that works for me
4.brief: A friend is struggling with stress and sleep. Write an email describing your own daily routine and why it works.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo estresado describiendo tu rutina diaria y por qué te funciona.
criteria: Three reduced time clauses with -ing or past participles.
Two clauses of condition (as long as, provided that, unless).
Use “creature of habit”, “to sleep in” and “to power through”.
4.model:
Hi Juanita,

I'm sorry to hear you're not sleeping well. I used to have the same problem, so let me tell you what works for me. I've become a real creature of habit!

I get up at 6 every day, even on weekends, because I've found that sleeping in on Sundays makes Mondays terrible. After getting up, I drink a big glass of water and go for a 20-minute walk. Before starting work, I write a list of three priorities. While working, I take a short break every hour; it stops me from feeling shattered by the afternoon.

In the past, I used to power through until midnight with coffee, but that was a disaster. Now, unless there's an emergency, I stop working at 7 p.m. After having dinner, I read or listen to music to wind down. As long as I'm in bed by 10:30, I feel great the next day.

Try it for two weeks and tell me how it goes!

Hugs,
Mariana

4.title: Should school start later?
4.brief: Write an essay discussing whether secondary schools should start later in the morning (e.g. at 9 a.m. instead of 6:30 a.m.).
4.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo sobre si los colegios deberían empezar más tarde en la mañana.
criteria: Four clauses of reason and condition (because, since, as, if, unless, provided that).
Two reduced time or reason clauses (Having slept…, Being tired…).
Clear paragraphs and a conclusion that answers the question.
4.model:
In Colombia, many secondary school students start classes at 6:30 a.m., which means getting up before five. Some experts argue that this is harmful and that schools should start later.

The main argument for a later start is biological. Since teenagers' body clocks naturally shift during puberty, most of them cannot fall asleep before 11 p.m. Arriving at school after only five hours of sleep, they are groggy and unable to concentrate. Studies in the USA show that, provided that schools start after 8:30, students get better grades and have fewer car accidents.

However, there are practical problems. Many parents work early, so they would have nobody to take their children to school. In addition, if schools finished later, students would have less time for sports and homework in the afternoon. Unless the transport system changes, a later start could also create more traffic.

Having considered both sides, I believe a later start is a good idea, as the benefits for students' health and learning are too important to ignore. Nevertheless, it should be introduced gradually, so that families and cities can adapt.

4.title: Sleep habits of Year 11 students
4.brief: Write a report for the head teacher on the sleep habits of a group of students. Present the findings and make recommendations.
4.briefEs: Escribe un informe para la directora sobre los hábitos de sueño de un grupo de estudiantes: hallazgos y recomendaciones.
criteria: Use at least three reduced time clauses (After finishing…, Before going to bed…, While studying…).
Use at least three clauses of reason or condition (since, unless, as long as, provided that).
Use the headings Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion, and two idioms from the unit (wind down, burn the midnight oil, hit the sack).
4.model:
Report: Sleep Habits of Year 11 Students

Introduction
This report analyses the sleep habits of sixty Year 11 students, based on a two-week diary.

Findings
Most students go to bed after midnight. After finishing their homework, many keep using their phones, so they rarely wind down before sleeping. Since lessons start at seven, the average student sleeps only six hours. Students who sleep less than seven hours reported feeling tired in class on most days. Several students admit burning the midnight oil before exams, although they feel exhausted the next day.

Recommendations
Before going to bed, students should switch off their screens for thirty minutes. As long as teachers avoid setting homework after eight, students could hit the sack earlier. Unless the timetable changes, the problem will probably continue.

Conclusion
While studying, students often forget that rest is part of learning. The solution is not difficult, but it needs everyone's cooperation. Provided that the school acts, sleep could improve within a month.

4.title: Flexible start times at the office
4.brief: Write a proposal to your company's management for flexible start times, explaining the current situation and the conditions of your plan.
4.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a la gerencia de tu empresa para horarios de entrada flexibles, explicando la situación actual y las condiciones del plan.
criteria: Use at least three reduced time or reason clauses (Having left…, After testing…, Being able to…).
Use at least three clauses of condition or reason (provided that, unless, as long as, since).
Use the headings Introduction, Current situation, Proposal and Conclusion.
4.model:
Proposal: Flexible Start Times at Andina Design

Introduction
This proposal suggests introducing flexible start times, based on a staff survey of forty employees.

Current situation
At present, everyone must arrive at eight. Since many employees live far from the office, they spend up to two hours commuting. Having left home at six, they are often tired by midday. Several employees told us they sometimes miss family time because of the long journey. Some colleagues, however, do their best work late in the day, whereas others are most productive before breakfast.

Proposal
We recommend allowing employees to start between seven and ten, provided that they work eight hours and attend the core meetings from eleven to one. Unless there is an urgent deadline, nobody would be required to stay late. After testing the system for three months, management could decide whether to keep it.

Conclusion
Being able to choose their hours would reduce stress and improve morale. As long as customer service remains covered, the company has little to lose.

4.title: NightOwl: a sleep app worth trying?
4.brief: Write a review of an app or gadget that claims to improve sleep or daily routines. Say how it works, what is good and bad, and whether you recommend it.
4.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una aplicación o dispositivo que promete mejorar el sueño o la rutina: cómo funciona, lo bueno y lo malo, y si lo recomiendas.
criteria: Use at least three reduced time clauses (After downloading…, While using…, Since starting…).
Use at least three clauses of condition (unless, provided that, as long as).
Use at least one idiom from the unit (wind down, hit the sack) and end with a rating.
4.model:
NightOwl: a sleep app worth trying?

NightOwl is a free app that records how well you sleep and suggests a bedtime routine. I have used it for a month, and my verdict is mostly positive.

After downloading it, you answer ten short questions about your habits. The app then creates a plan that helps you wind down: soft music, a reminder to switch off screens and a countdown to bedtime. Since I started following the plan, I have been going to bed at eleven instead of one in the morning.

However, the app has weaknesses. Unless you pay for the premium version, you can only see the last three nights. Also, some of the advice is obvious, such as "avoid coffee in the evening". While using it, I noticed that the sleep score changed even when I slept the same hours.

Overall, it is a useful tool, provided that you do not take the numbers too seriously. As long as you want a gentle push to hit the sack earlier, I recommend it. Three and a half stars out of five.

4.title: Longer opening hours for the library
4.brief: Write a formal letter asking the university library to stay open later during the exam period. Give your reasons and explain under what conditions it would work.
4.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal pidiendo que la biblioteca universitaria abra hasta más tarde en época de exámenes: razones y condiciones.
criteria: Use at least two reduced time clauses (After studying…, Having…) and one indirect question.
Use at least three clauses of reason or condition (since, provided that, unless, as long as).
Start with “Dear Sir or Madam”, end with “Yours faithfully” and make a clear request.
4.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to ask whether the university library could stay open until midnight during the exam period.

As a third-year student, I spend most of my free time preparing for exams. Since the library closes at eight, many of us have to study at home, where it is hard to concentrate. After studying all day in a noisy flat, I often feel exhausted. Moreover, several classmates who live far from the campus have no quiet place to study at all.

I understand that longer hours mean extra costs. However, provided that the library opens only during the three weeks before exams, the expense would be small. Unless students can study in a quiet place, they will keep struggling at home, and their results may suffer.

I would be grateful if you could consider this request and let me know your decision by the end of the month. I am happy to organise a petition if that would help.

Yours faithfully,
Camila Ríos

4.title: The night before the exam
4.brief: Write a short story about a night when you (or a character) stayed up studying and what happened the next day.
4.briefEs: Escribe un relato corto sobre una noche de estudio hasta tarde y lo que ocurrió al día siguiente.
criteria: Use at least three reduced time clauses (After making…, Feeling…, Having slept…, While reading…).
Use at least two clauses of reason or condition (since, as long as, unless).
Use two idioms from the unit (burn the midnight oil, hit the sack) and include some dialogue.
4.model:
At nine o'clock the night before my chemistry exam, I realised I had studied only half of the book. After making a huge pot of coffee, I decided to burn the midnight oil.

By midnight, the words were dancing on the page. Since I could not concentrate, I picked up my phone and watched videos for an hour. Feeling guilty, I put it away and tried again.

At two in the morning, my mother appeared at the door, holding a glass of milk. "Having slept only three hours a night all week, you won't remember anything tomorrow," she said. "Go and hit the sack." I argued, but she turned off the light.

The next morning, I woke up calm. While reading the first question, I was surprised to find that I knew the answer. I realised that, as long as I slept enough, my brain would do the work for me.

I got an eight out of ten. Since then, I have never studied after midnight.

4.title: The new night shift
4.brief: Write an email to a team announcing a new night shift. Explain the conditions and give advice on adapting to the change.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un equipo anunciando un nuevo turno de noche: condiciones y consejos para adaptarse al cambio.
criteria: Use at least three reduced time clauses (After completing…, While working…, Before starting…).
Use at least three clauses of reason or condition (since, unless, provided that, as long as).
Use at least one idiom from the unit (wind down, hit the sack) and a professional opening and closing.
4.model:
Dear team,

I am writing to explain the new schedule for the night shift, which starts on 1 June.

Since the number of online orders has doubled, we need people to prepare packages between ten at night and six in the morning. Unless we find enough volunteers, we will have to assign the shifts by rotation.

After completing a week of nights, you will receive two days off in a row. Provided that you tell your supervisor in advance, you can also swap shifts with a colleague. While working at night, you may take a thirty-minute break whenever the workload is low.

I know that changing sleep patterns is not easy. Before starting your first shift, try to go to bed later during the previous days, and wind down with a warm shower instead of screens when you get home.

Please reply by Friday if you would like to volunteer. Your supervisor will share the full timetable on Monday.

Best wishes,
Marta Ibáñez

5.title: Straight talkers vs diplomats
5.brief: Is it better to be outspoken or tactful? Write an essay discussing both communication styles at work and in personal life.
5.briefEs: ¿Es mejor ser directo o diplomático? Escribe un ensayo sobre ambos estilos en el trabajo y la vida personal.
criteria: Three “It’s + adjective / noun + infinitive” structures (It’s important to…, It’s a mistake to…).
Three gerunds as subjects (Being honest is…).
Four expressions from the unit (to beat around the bush, candid, to sugar-coat…).
5.model:
Some people believe that honesty is always the best policy, while others prefer to soften difficult messages. Both communication styles have advantages and disadvantages.

Outspoken people get straight to the point. At work, this can be very efficient: it's a waste of time to beat around the bush when a project is failing. Being candid also builds trust, because colleagues know exactly what you think. However, it's easy to hurt people's feelings if you don't mince your words, and in a culture like Colombia's, where relationships matter a lot, this can damage your reputation.

Tactful people, on the other hand, know how to read between the lines and choose their words carefully. Criticising someone gently is more likely to produce positive change than attacking them. The danger is that being too diplomatic can lead to confusion. If you sugar-coat everything, people may not realise there is a problem at all.

In my opinion, it's essential to combine both styles. Being honest about the facts and kind in the way you express them is the most effective approach. After all, it's not what you say, but how you say it.

5.title: Feedback for a colleague
5.brief: Write an email giving feedback to a colleague who often talks over people in meetings. Be honest but tactful.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo con retroalimentación a un colega que interrumpe en las reuniones: sé honesto pero diplomático.
criteria: Two “It’s + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Two gerunds as subjects.
Use “to talk over someone”, “to come across as” and “tactful”.
5.model:
Hi Daniel,

I hope you don't mind me writing to you about something I noticed in yesterday's meeting. I'm sharing it because I value working with you.

Your ideas about the new campaign were excellent, and it's clear that you know the market very well. However, at times you talked over other people, especially Laura and Felipe. I'm sure it wasn't intentional, but interrupting colleagues can make you come across as impatient, even when you're just enthusiastic.

It's important for everyone to feel heard, particularly the new members of the team. Letting people finish their points usually makes meetings shorter, not longer, and listening first might also give you more information to support your arguments.

One idea that helps me is writing down my thoughts while others are speaking, then sharing them when there's a pause. It's a simple trick, but it works.

I hope this is useful. I'd be happy to talk about it over coffee if you like, and please tell me if there's anything I could improve too.

Best,
Mónica

5.title: Lost in communication
5.brief: Write a story about a misunderstanding caused by different communication styles (between friends, family or colleagues from different cultures).
5.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre un malentendido causado por estilos de comunicación diferentes.
criteria: Two gerunds as subjects and two “It’s + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Use “to talk at cross purposes” and “to read between the lines”.
A clear beginning, problem and resolution.
5.model:
When my company sent me to work in Amsterdam, I thought the hardest thing would be the weather. I was wrong.

In my first meeting, I presented a marketing plan. My Dutch manager, Pieter, said: "This part doesn't work. It's confusing." I was shocked. In Colombia, it's unusual to criticise someone so directly, especially in public. I spent the whole night thinking he wanted to fire me.

The next day, I asked him if I should look for another job. He looked completely confused. We had been talking at cross purposes: for him, saying "it doesn't work" was just a normal comment. For me, it sounded like a disaster. He explained that being direct is a sign of respect in the Netherlands.

I realised that I had been trying to read between the lines when there was nothing between the lines! Learning to accept candid feedback took me months, but it made me a better professional. Now, when I return to Colombia, it's my turn to remember that being too direct can sound rude here.

5.title: A communication workshop for team leaders
5.brief: Write a proposal to the human resources director for a workshop that helps team leaders give feedback clearly and kindly.
5.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a la directora de recursos humanos para un taller que ayude a los líderes de equipo a dar retroalimentación con claridad y amabilidad.
criteria: Use at least three “It + adjective + infinitive” structures, one with “for + person” (It is important for managers to…).
Use at least three gerunds as subjects (Receiving vague comments is…).
Use at least two expressions from the unit (to beat around the bush, to come across as, candid, tactful) and the headings Introduction, Current situation, Proposal and Conclusion.
5.model:
Proposal: A Communication Workshop for Team Leaders

Introduction
This proposal recommends a one-day workshop on clear and respectful communication, based on interviews with twelve team leaders.

Current situation
Many leaders say it is difficult to give negative feedback without upsetting people. Some beat around the bush, so employees do not understand what to improve. Others are too blunt and come across as unfriendly. Receiving vague comments is frustrating, while hearing harsh ones can destroy motivation.

Proposal
The workshop would teach leaders how to be candid yet tactful. Practising real situations in small groups is the most effective method, so each participant would role-play two conversations. Each session would last ninety minutes, and a short report would be shared afterwards. It is important for managers to listen before speaking, and it would be useful for them to receive feedback from a trained coach.

Conclusion
Improving communication is not expensive, and it is worth the effort. It would be a mistake to ignore a problem that affects every team.

5.title: Communication in weekly team meetings
5.brief: Write a report on a survey about how people communicate in team meetings. Present the findings and recommend changes.
5.briefEs: Escribe un informe sobre una encuesta acerca de cómo se comunica la gente en las reuniones de equipo: resultados y cambios recomendados.
criteria: Use at least three “It + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Use at least three gerunds as subjects (Being interrupted is…).
Use at least two expressions from the unit (to talk over someone, candid) and the headings Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
5.model:
Report: Communication in Weekly Team Meetings

Introduction
This report summarises the results of a survey of thirty employees about the way we communicate in weekly meetings.

Findings
Being interrupted is the main complaint: sixteen employees said that colleagues often talk over them. Speaking up in front of the manager is also difficult for newer staff, and many find it hard to disagree openly. Only four people said they felt comfortable giving their opinion. On the other hand, most people appreciate candid feedback, provided that it is given kindly. Asking questions is seen as a sign of weakness by about a third of the group.

Recommendations
It is essential for the chair to give everyone a turn. It would also be useful for each meeting to end with five minutes of open questions. Writing a short agenda in advance helps people prepare.

Conclusion
It is not difficult to improve meetings; however, it takes commitment from everyone to listen properly.

5.title: Say It Straight: a podcast for better conversations
5.brief: Write a review of a podcast, book or video series about communication. Describe the content, give your opinion and recommend it (or not).
5.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un pódcast, libro o serie de videos sobre comunicación: contenido, opinión y recomendación.
criteria: Use at least three “It + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Use at least two gerunds as subjects (Listening to real stories is…).
Use at least three expressions from the unit (to read between the lines, to sugar-coat, tactful, to talk over someone, to come across as) and end with a rating.
5.model:
Say It Straight: a podcast for better conversations

Say It Straight is a weekly podcast in which a psychologist and a journalist discuss how people communicate at work and at home. I have listened to it for three months, and I highly recommend it.

Each episode is about thirty minutes long. Listening to real stories from callers is what makes the show different: you hear a manager who comes across as cold, or a daughter who cannot read between the lines of her father's silence. It is fascinating to hear how small changes in wording can transform a conversation.

The presenters are tactful but candid, and they never sugar-coat their advice. It is refreshing for a podcast to admit that some conflicts have no easy solution.

On the negative side, it is sometimes hard to follow the debates because the two hosts talk over each other. Also, answering listeners' questions takes up too much time in later episodes.

Overall, this is an intelligent, warm show. I give it four stars out of five.

5.title: Contradictory answers from a helpline
5.brief: Write a formal letter of complaint about a company whose staff gave you contradictory information and treated you rudely. Request a written reply.
5.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de queja a una empresa cuyo personal te dio información contradictoria y te trató mal. Solicita una respuesta por escrito.
criteria: Use at least three “It + adjective + infinitive” structures (It is frustrating to…, It is unacceptable for…).
Use at least two gerunds as subjects (Being transferred… made me feel…).
Use “to come across as” once, start with “Dear Sir or Madam” and end with “Yours faithfully”.
5.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the lack of clear communication from your customer service department regarding my mobile phone contract.

Over the last month, I have called your helpline four times to ask about an extra charge on my bill. It is frustrating to receive a different answer every time. The first adviser said the charge was an error, whereas the second told me it was part of my plan. Being transferred between departments without any explanation made me feel that nobody wanted to take responsibility.

The third adviser, who came across as impatient, interrupted me and refused to listen to my explanation. It is unacceptable for a customer to be treated in this way. Receiving a written explanation would be much better than another phone call.

I therefore request that someone with authority contact me in writing within seven working days, explain the charge and correct my bill if necessary. It would be helpful for you to confirm the name of the person who will deal with my case.

Yours faithfully,
Óscar Beltrán

5.title: Five tips for emails that get answers
5.brief: Write a short article for a workplace newsletter with five tips for writing emails that people read and answer.
5.briefEs: Escribe un artículo breve para un boletín laboral con cinco consejos para escribir correos que la gente lea y responda.
criteria: Use at least three “It + adjective / noun + infinitive” structures (It is a mistake to…, It is easy to…).
Use at least three gerunds as subjects (Beating around the bush wastes…, Being tactful costs…).
Use at least three expressions from the unit (to beat around the bush, to come across as, to sugar-coat, candid, tactful) and give exactly five tips.
5.model:
Five Tips for Emails That Get Answers

We send dozens of emails a day, yet many of them are ignored. Here is how to improve yours.

First, be clear. It is a mistake to bury your request in the fifth paragraph. Beating around the bush wastes your reader's time, so state what you need in the first two sentences.

Second, choose a suitable tone. It is easy to come across as rude when writing quickly, especially if you leave out greetings. Being tactful costs nothing: "Could you possibly send…?" sounds far friendlier than "Send me…".

Third, do not sugar-coat bad news, but explain it kindly. Colleagues generally prefer a candid message to a vague one.

Fourth, keep it short. It is better for the reader to scan five lines than to read twenty. Using bullet points can help.

Finally, read your message before sending it. Checking for mistakes takes thirty seconds, and it is worth doing.

5.title: Texting or talking?
5.brief: Write an argumentative essay on whether text messages are damaging face-to-face communication among young people.
5.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo argumentativo sobre si los mensajes de texto dañan la comunicación cara a cara entre los jóvenes.
criteria: Use at least three “It + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Use at least three gerunds as subjects (Reading between the lines is…, Being able to think… helps…).
Organise the essay in an introduction, one paragraph for each side and a conclusion, and use “to read between the lines” and “to come across as”.
5.model:
Many teenagers now prefer sending messages to speaking face to face. Some adults claim that texting is destroying real conversation. In my opinion, this view is partly true, but also exaggerated.

On the one hand, it is easy to misunderstand a written message. Without a voice or a facial expression, a short reply such as "fine" can come across as angry. Reading between the lines is difficult when you cannot see the other person. Moreover, hiding behind a screen makes it tempting to be rude.

On the other hand, texting has clear benefits. It is convenient for shy people to express themselves calmly, and sending a quick message is often more polite than calling someone at a bad moment. Being able to think before answering also helps people avoid saying things they regret.

In conclusion, it is unwise to blame technology for poor communication. What matters is choosing the right channel for each situation: it is best to talk in person about serious problems, and to text about simple arrangements.

6.title: A news report
6.brief: Write a news report about a story that turned out to be false or exaggerated. Explain how it started and what has happened since.
6.briefEs: Escribe una noticia sobre una historia falsa o exagerada: cómo empezó y qué ha pasado desde entonces.
criteria: Correct contrast of present perfect, present perfect continuous and simple past.
Two past perfect verbs with time adverbs (by then, already, just).
Four words from the unit (rumour, unsubstantiated, to corroborate, to blow out of proportion…).
6.model:
"Shark" in Bogotá Lake Was a Plastic Toy

A rumour that a shark was living in a lake in a Bogotá park turned out to be completely false, police confirmed yesterday.

The story began last Saturday, when a teenager posted a blurry video on TikTok. By Sunday morning, the video had already been viewed more than two million times, and several news websites had published the story without checking it. Hundreds of curious people went to the park, and the city government closed the area for safety reasons.

On Tuesday, divers searched the lake and found a large plastic shark attached to a remote-controlled boat. The teenager has since admitted that it was a joke. "I didn't think anyone would believe it," he told reporters.

Experts have been warning for years about the dangers of sharing unsubstantiated stories online. "Nobody tried to corroborate the video with a second source," said journalism professor Clara Ruiz. "A simple joke was blown out of proportion in a few hours."

The park has now reopened, but some websites have been criticised for publishing the story. Several of them have apologised and removed their articles.

6.title: What's been going on?
6.brief: Write an email to a friend you haven't seen for a long time. Tell him or her what has happened, what you have been doing recently and what had happened before you last met.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un viejo amigo con lo que ha pasado, lo que has estado haciendo y lo que había pasado antes.
criteria: Two present perfect and two present perfect continuous verbs.
Two simple past verbs with specific times and one past perfect.
